angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 19,408,639 km at 82.99 pc = 3.13 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114341: distance 82.988 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.018), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 82.988 +/- 1.494 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 12.6710 +/- 0.2225 mas (same row, RUWE 2.39), 57.0 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 27.898 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114341: radius 27.898 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 290.845 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.058) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 19,408,639 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4516 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114341: effective temperature 4516 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.068) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 114341: effective temperature 4516 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.068) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Burnashev (1985), Abastumani Astrophys. Obs. Bull. 59, 83; VizieR III/126, part2 record 299 (BS 8812)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
